questions.question: Define natural resources and distinguish between renewable and non-renewable resources, with examples.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources are materials and features of nature that people use (water, air, soil, sunlight, plants, animals, minerals, fossil fuels). Renewable: can be replaced naturally within a human lifetime or never run out if used carefully - sunlight, wind, water, forests, fish, soil (though they can be damaged by overuse). Non-renewable: cannot be replaced or take millions of years to form - coal, oil, natural gas, gold, platinum, diamonds.

questions.question: Explain why water, air and soil are essential, and why South Africa must use them carefully.
questions.expected_answer: Water: all life needs it (drinking, sanitation, farming, industry, electricity); only about 3% of water is fresh and less than 1% easily available; SA is water-scarce (about 450-500 mm average rainfall). Air: oxygen for breathing, CO2 for photosynthesis, protection from radiation, warmth. Soil: food production; forms very slowly (100+ years per cm); only about 13% of SA land is arable.

questions.question: Describe how people abuse water, air and soil, and suggest ways to protect soil.
questions.expected_answer: Water: pollution by sewage, fertilisers and pesticides, factory waste, acid mine drainage, litter/plastic; waste through leaks. Air: pollution from coal power stations (Mpumalanga), factories, vehicles, household fires, burning rubbish, mine dust - causes asthma and climate change. Soil: erosion from overgrazing, deforestation, ploughing down slopes, frequent burning (dongas, silted dams); chemical pollution, salinisation, monoculture, desertification. Protection: contour ploughing, terracing, planting vegetation, rotational grazing, fewer animals, crop rotation, compost and mulch, no-till.
